payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is there image-grounded evidence of any progress toward rendering the content as a pencil drawing, even if the transformation is incomplete?
node.criteria: Pass if the image shows some visible pencil-drawing-style treatment of its content, including an incomplete treatment; fail if sufficient evidence shows no requested transformation has progressed; unknown if evidence is insufficient to determine whether any such progress occurred. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
node.binding: Assess only visible changes in the supplied image that move its visual content toward a pencil-drawn style; do not infer progress from unrelated changes.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows a visible pencil-drawing-style treatment across the scene: colors are muted, edges and textures appear sketch-like, and the food and surrounding objects have a drawn, grainy appearance compared with the source. This is evidence of progress toward the requested style.

The edited image visibly applies a muted, grainy pencil-like treatment across the food and surrounding objects, indicating progress toward a pencil drawing, though the result retains some color and photographic shading.

The edited image has a visibly muted, gray-toned, grainy treatment with softened colors and sketch-like shading across the food and surrounding objects, showing progress toward a pencil-drawing style.

The edited image shows a visible pencil-drawing-style treatment across the scene: colors are muted and surfaces have a grainy, sketch-like appearance with softened outlines. This is evidence of progress toward the requested style.
The edited image has a visibly muted, gray-toned, grainy treatment with softened outlines across the food and surrounding objects, consistent with some pencil-drawing-style rendering.

fulfillment: The node’s binding asks whether the image *visibly appears as a completed pencil drawing*, but its criteria make completion equivalent to s1 passing. That collapses the distinction between partial progress and fulfillment: all five traces call the muted, grainy, sketch-like treatment complete, despite one noting retained color and photographic shading, while s2 describes progress. Refine the completion criterion so it independently tests whether the overall image reads as a pencil drawing rather than merely showing pencil-like effects; use s2 only as evidence of progress, not as a substitute for that judgment. Require the node to reconcile conflicting cues and cite visible evidence for both the drawing treatment and any remaining photographic/color appearance before deciding. Preserve the existing partial/absent/unknown routing and do not force the reference label: the image shows substantial style change, but the traces do not establish that it is fully a pencil drawing. No transport, schema, or dependency failures are reported; this is a semantic threshold and evidence-composition problem.
